name: Results called stale when what they measure did not change
problem: A recorded result is called stale when any file of the repository's measured code changed, so every component's metrics are re-run after every commit although what most of them measure did not change. The reruns cost time and money, and people learn to ignore the staleness test or to stop running metrics.
who_has_it: Maintainers and AI agents who commit often, and whoever pays for a re-run.
why_it_matters: A result that still describes the code it measured is current evidence, and re-measuring it repeats what is known. When code changes many times a day, a rule that stales everything turns each commit into a full re-run or into a habit of not checking.
why_hard: What a result measures is not written in the result: it depends on which files the arm's module reads, which of them are shared, and which cases it runs. A rule narrow enough to save reruns can keep a result whose measured code changed, which is worse than a rerun.
existing_attempts: Staling every result when any measured file changed (one list of code paths for the whole repository), and re-recording by hand when someone remembers.
